subject.title: feat(gmail): add --inline and --text content modes to gmail attachment

question: Should core `gog` own PDF and text extraction for attacker-controlled Gmail attachments, or should this PR be narrowed to the parser-free `--inline` mode?
rationale: The implementation is now bounded, killable, tested, and proven, so the remaining blocker is not a mechanical defect; it is whether the repository wants a third-party document parser and hidden subprocess within its permanent core trust boundary.

options.title: Land inline only
options.body: Split out `--text` and merge the parser-free base64 transport mode that directly solves remote filesystem isolation.

options.title: Accept core extraction
options.body: Keep both modes and explicitly own the pinned PDF parser, subprocess protocol, resource limits, and future parser security updates in core.

recommendation.title: Land inline only
recommendation.body: Split out `--text` and merge the parser-free base64 transport mode that directly solves remote filesystem isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-wide product and trust-boundary decision rather than a remaining line-level Gmail defect.
